abstract: BACKGROUND: Mirror syndrome is associated with both nonimmune and immune hydrops fetalis. The clinical manifestations are quite varied, and the pathophysiology is poorly understood. We describe a case of mirror syndrome associated with afetus that had a rapidly growing sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) without overt hydrops. CASE: At 30 weeks' gestational age a fetus with SCT began to show early sonographic evidence of right heart failure, placentomegaly and polyhydramnios without overt fetal hydrops. Shortly after these findings were noted, the mother began to develop hypertension, epigastric pain, proteinuria and thrombocytopenia. These findings were all reversed after delivery of the fetus. Subsequent surgery on the infant was successful. CONCLUSION: Mirror syndrome has been linked with SCT and is usually associated with severe fetal hydropic changes. In our case the development of mirror syndrome preceded the manifestations of overt hydrops. Identification of early signs of fetal compromise or hydrops may help to predict patients who will develop mirror syndrome and improve outcomes with earlier intervention.
abstract_ja: 背景：ミラー症候群は非免疫性および免疫性の胎児水腫に関連します。臨床像は多様で、病態生理は十分に解明されていません。症例：妊娠30週において、急速に増大する仙尾部奇形腫(SCT)を有する胎児が、明らかな水腫を伴わずに右心不全、胎盤腫大、羊水過多の早期超音波所見を示しました。これらの所見の直後に、母体は高血圧、心窩部痛、蛋白尿、血小板減少を発症しました。これらの所見は分娩後にすべて改善しました。その後、新生児の手術は成功しました。結論：ミラー症候群はSCTと関連が報告されており、通常は重度の胎児水腫性変化を伴います。本症例では、明らかな水腫の出現に先立ってミラー症候群が発症しました。胎児の危険徴候や水腫の早期兆候を把握することは、ミラー症候群を発症する患者の予測に役立ち、より早期の介入により予後を改善する可能性があります。
